segments.oily: One reviewer notes the formula is oil-free and does not make her oily, and it is described as suitable for oily skin types.
segments.dry: One reviewer with dry skin found the consistency slightly oily in a way that felt nice on her skin, and another reports the stick made her skin less dry and sun-damaged.
segments.sensitive: Several reviewers with sensitive skin report no irritation and appreciate the fragrance-free, non-comedogenic formula.
segments.mature: One reviewer used it around the eye area with no stinging, though skin was not explicitly called mature; not enough distinct mature-skin material beyond this.
segments.combination: One reviewer with combination skin has generally moved away from physical sunscreens and finds this one only average, expecting to return to chemical formulas.

concerns.spots: One reviewer uses it on the hands specifically to help keep dark spots at bay.
concerns.blemishes: One reviewer with a history of clogged pores and breakouts calls it a holy grail that doesn't cause breakouts; no dissent reported.
concerns.oiliness: Reviewers report the formula is oil-free, non-greasy and does not add shine, with one noting it is suitable for oily skin.
concerns.redness: One reviewer notes it doesn't sting the eyes and is gentle, but broader redness-specific reports are limited.
concerns.barrier: Reviewers with sensitive or reactive skin report no irritation and describe the formula as gentle and non-comedogenic.
concerns.aging: One reviewer highlights the inclusion of Vitamin C and E as a plus but does not describe a visible anti-aging effect.

extraits.texte: This is an ok sunscreen. Don't expect it to be transparent or to blend well unless you really rub it in. If you wear the required amount of sunscreen no physical sunscreen will be invisible especially for darker skin tones. Good if you're going to be outdoors and don't care if your sunscreen looks aesthetically pleasing. I've given up on physical sunscreens and will stick to combination sunscreens.
